get.description: Checks that the API is reachable. Not needed before other calls.

Up to three reports this Book can have, each as a request a person would type and its `intent`, chosen by fixed rules from the Book’s groups and data. Use them when the person does not know what to ask, or after `not_a_report`; to build one, send its `intent` (no AI) and, to show it, `format: html` to `POST /api/v1/books/{bookId}/report`. Read-only.

post.summary: Build a financial report of a Book from a request in any language
post.description:
Builds a financial report of the Book: of one of its root groups (such as Expenses or Assets, with its subgroups and Accounts) or of income versus expenses, over a period of whole months, by month or not, optionally only for `#hashtags`. Read-only: the Book is never changed.

To show a person a report, send `{ "prompt": "<their request, in their own words and language>", "format": "html" }` and give them the returned HTML file as it is: it is self-contained and interactive. With the Bkper CLI: `bkper app api request report /api/v1/books/<bookId>/report -d '{"prompt":"…","format":"html"}' > report.html`, then publish `report.html`.

With `format: spec` (the default) the report is JSON: its spec, intent, language, query, data time and link. An `intent`, such as a suggestion’s or a previous report’s, builds the report without AI.

Numbers are computed by deterministic code from the Book’s balances, which may be up to 60 seconds old; AI only reads the prompt to choose the group, period and view among the Book’s own.

parameters.name: bookId
parameters.description: Id of the Book, as Bkper gives it (`bkper book list`).

200.description: The report: one self-contained HTML file (`format: html`), or JSON with its spec, intent, language, query and link (`format: spec`)

schema.description: With `format: html`: a self-contained, interactive HTML document of the report, in `language`. Every script and style is inline and it loads nothing, so it works in a sandboxed frame: the chart shows tooltips, rows open in place, and a link opens the report in the Report app.

403.description: The person cannot view the Book (`forbidden`)

404.description: Book not found, or not shared with the person (`book_not_found`)

422.description: Not a report this Book can have (`not_a_report`, with `suggestions` to offer instead), a period that has not started (`future_period`), or an intent whose root is not a root group of the Book (`unknown_root`)

429.description: The person’s Bkper AI allowance is used up (`ai_allowance_exhausted`); requests by `intent` still work

502.description: Bkper or Bkper AI failed; try again (`upstream_error`)

code.description: What failed: `invalid_request` (400, the message names the field), `unauthorized` (401, no valid Bkper token), `forbidden` (403, the person cannot view the Book), `not_found` (404, no such API route), `book_not_found` (404, no such Book, or not shared with the person), `not_a_report` (422, the request names nothing this Book can report: ask for a root group or income versus expenses with a period, or use a suggestion), `future_period` (422, the period has not started), `unknown_root` (422, the intent names no root group of the Book), `ai_allowance_exhausted` (429, the person’s Bkper AI allowance is used up: requests by `intent` still work), `upstream_error` (502, Bkper or Bkper AI failed: try again) or `internal_error` (500).

message.description: What failed, in English, for people and logs. Never the request text.
message.example: Book not found, or not shared with you.

suggestions.description: Up to three reports, chosen from the Book’s own groups and data.

text.description: The report as a person would ask for it, in the requested language.

Suggestion.description: A report this Book can have. Send its `intent` to `POST /api/v1/books/{bookId}/report` to build it without AI.

root.description: Id of a root (top-level) group of the Book, as in `bkper group list`, or `net-result` for income versus expenses (every Incoming root versus every Outgoing root).

period.description: The period, in the Book’s time zone: `today`, `this_month`, `last_month`, `this_quarter`, `last_quarter`, `this_year`, `last_year`, `ytd`, `last_12_months`, `all`, a year (`2025`), a quarter (`2025-Q3`) or a month (`2025-10`). Current periods end today; past ones are whole calendar periods.

monthly.description: Show the period month by month.

view.description: The layout asked for: `trend` (over time), `breakdown` (by subgroups and Accounts) or `total` (the amount alone). Left out, the report picks one.

chart.description: The chart the person asked for: `pie` (the parts of the total), `stacked` (the parts by month), `area` (by month), `compare` (each part against the previous period), `waterfall` (a bridge: from Incoming to the net result through each Outgoing Account, or from the previous position through each part’s change), `table` (no chart) or `auto`. Left out or `auto`, the report picks one; a chart that does not fit the report falls back to the one the report picks (see the response’s `chart`).

hashtags.description: Only transactions with all these hashtags, without `#`.

ReportIntent.description: Exactly what to report, with no AI needed: a root group or `net-result`, a period, whether by month, an optional view, chart and hashtags. Take it from a suggestion or from an earlier report’s `intent`.

language.description: The Bkper language of the report’s texts.

query.description: The Bkper query of exactly the report’s transactions and dates, to list them or check balances in Bkper.

dataAt.description: When the balances were read (ISO 8601); they may be up to 60 seconds old.

kind.description: The chart in the spec: `bar`, `line`, `area` or `stacked` by month; `ranked-bar`, `donut` or `pie` of the parts; `compare` (each part against the previous period); `waterfall` (a bridge); `none` for no chart.

fallback.description: True when the intent’s `chart` does not fit this report, so `kind` is the chart the report picks instead.

chart.description: The chart drawn, and whether the one asked for fit.

url.description: The same report in the Report app, to open or share with the person.

ReportSpec.description: The report as a flat json-render spec (`root` and `elements`) of the Report catalog, every text in `language`: `Report` (title, period) holds `Answer` (amount, previous period amount and change; for a net result, Incoming and Outgoing), `Chart` (when one fits), `BreakdownTable` (rows of subgroups and Accounts with amount, share and change, nested) and `Source`. Amounts and ratios are exact decimal strings; months and instants are ISO.

suggestions.description: With `not_a_report`: reports this Book can have, to offer the person instead.

prompt.description: The report the person asked for, in their own words and language: do not translate it. Include what they said about the period, the view and `#hashtags`; leave out the Book’s name or id, which the path gives. Uses one Bkper AI decision.
prompt.example: show my expenses by category this year

language.description: Language of the report’s texts, as a BCP 47 tag of one of the 133 Bkper languages, such as `pt` or `pt-BR`. Leave it out to write the report in the language of `prompt`, else `Accept-Language`, else English.

format.description: What to return. `html` to show the report to a person: one self-contained, interactive HTML file (`text/html`) that loads nothing and links to the report in the Report app; save it and publish or share it as it is. `spec` (the default) for JSON: the report as a json-render spec with its intent, language, query, data time and link.

ReportRequest.description: Exactly one of `prompt` (the person’s request, in any language) or `intent` (from a suggestion or an earlier report, with no AI). Usually `{ "prompt": "…", "format": "html" }`.
